body:
<!-- Before completing this template, read:
https://docs.sympy.org/dev/contributing/pull-request-guidelines.html
Local source: doc/src/contributing/pull-request-guidelines.rst
Keep all section headings below. -->

#### References to other Issues or PRs
No linked issue.
Found while testing edge cases myself.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed
convolution_fft([], [1, 2]) and convolution_ntt([], [1, 2], prime=...) return [0].
convolution([], [1, 2]) raises ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty.
Cause: the result length is computed as len(a) + len(b) - 1, which is 1 when one list is empty and the other has 2 items.
Fix in convolution_fft, convolution_ntt and convolution_int: return [] early if either input is empty.
Fix in convolution(): skip the zero padding when either list is empty.
File changed: sympy/discrete/convolutions.py, 11 lines added.

#### Other comments
Existing tests only covered [] with [] and [] with [1].
New test test_convolution_empty_input covers:
lengths 0 to 3, in both orders;
the prime, dyadic, subset and Rational paths;
non-empty inputs, which are unaffected.
The test fails before the fix and passes after it.
The cyclic case cycle=3 still returns [0, 0, 0].
sympy/discrete tests pass, and the doctests pass.

#### AI Generation Disclosure
AI helped find the bug by running edge-case tests.
AI wrote the first version of the fix and of the test.


<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* discrete
  * convolution functions no longer return [0] or raise an error when one input is empty.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

diff --git a/sympy/discrete/convolutions.py b/sympy/discrete/convolutions.py
index 5e50a70dbf39..daffcc840a7e 100644
--- a/sympy/discrete/convolutions.py
+++ b/sympy/discrete/convolutions.py
@@ -111,7 +111,8 @@ def loop(a):
                 (ia, ma), (ib, mb) = da, db
                 den = ma*mb
                 ls = convolution_int(ia, ib)
-                ls.extend([0]*(len(a) + len(b) - 1 - len(ls)))
+                if a and b:
+                    ls.extend([0]*(len(a) + len(b) - 1 - len(ls)))
                 if den != 1:
                     ls = [Rational(i, den) for i in ls]
         if ls is None:
@@ -159,6 +160,9 @@ def convolution_fft(a, b, dps=None):
 
     """
 
+    if not a or not b:
+        return []
+
     a, b = a[:], b[:]
     n = m = len(a) + len(b) - 1 # convolution size
 
@@ -214,6 +218,8 @@ def convolution_ntt(a, b, prime):
 
     """
 
+    if not a or not b:
+        return []
     a, b, p = a[:], b[:], as_int(prime)
     n = m = len(a) + len(b) - 1 # convolution size
 
@@ -568,6 +574,9 @@ def convolution_int(a, b):
            University of California, Berkeley, California (2004).
            https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~fateman/papers/polysbyGMP.pdf
     """
+    if not a or not b:
+        return []
+
     # An upper bound on the largest coefficient in p(x)q(x) is given by (1 + min(dp, dq))N(p)N(q)
     # where dp = deg(p), dq = deg(q), N(f) denotes the coefficient of largest modulus in f [1]
     B = max(abs(c) for c in a)*max(abs(c) for c in b)*(1 + min(len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1))
diff --git a/sympy/discrete/tests/test_convolutions.py b/sympy/discrete/tests/test_convolutions.py
index 6bef164b0400..26ef960a3210 100644
--- a/sympy/discrete/tests/test_convolutions.py
+++ b/sympy/discrete/tests/test_convolutions.py
@@ -176,6 +176,26 @@ def test_cyclic_convolution():
     raises(ValueError, lambda: convolution([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], cycle=-1))
 
 
+def test_convolution_empty_input():
+    # the convolution of an empty sequence with anything is empty
+    p = 19*2**10 + 1
+    for kwargs in ({}, {'prime': p}):
+        funcs = ((convolution, convolution_fft, convolution_int)
+                 if not kwargs else (convolution, convolution_ntt))
+        for func in funcs:
+            for seq in ([], [1], [1, 2], [1, 2, 3]):
+                assert func([], seq, **kwargs) == []
+                assert func(seq, [], **kwargs) == []
+    assert convolution([], [1, 2], cycle=3) == [0, 0, 0]
+    assert convolution([], [Rational(1, 2), 3]) == []
+    assert convolution([], [1, 2], dyadic=True) == []
+    assert convolution([], [1, 2], subset=True) == []
+    # a nonempty input is unaffected
+    assert convolution([1], [1, 2]) == [1, 2]
+    assert convolution_fft([1], [1, 2]) == [1, 2]
+    assert convolution_ntt([1], [1, 2], prime=p) == [1, 2]
+
+
 def test_convolution_fft():
     assert all(convolution_fft([], x, dps=y) == [] for x in ([], [1]) for y in (None, 3))
     assert convolution_fft([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) == [4, 13, 28, 27, 18]

```
Package: discrete.
Note: convolution functions no longer return [0] or raise an error when one input is empty.
```
You have to use a literal module name and note without prefix. The following should work.
```
* discrete
  * convolution functions no longer return [0] or raise an error when one input is empty.
```
